title: Averages

steps.title: Average means equal share
steps.content: The arithmetic average is the total of all values divided by the number of values. It is the value each item would have if the total were shared equally.
steps.formula: Average = Sum of values ÷ Number of values

steps.title: Find a simple average
steps.prompt: What is the average of 14, 18, 22 and 26?
steps.explanation: Sum = 80. There are 4 values, so average = 80/4 = 20.

steps.title: Use total = average × count
steps.content: In placement questions, it is often faster to work with totals. If the average of n numbers is A, their sum is n×A. When a value is replaced, update the total first.
steps.example: Average of 5 numbers is 16, so total = 80. Replace 12 by 22: new total = 90, new average = 90/5 = 18.
steps.tip: When one number is added or removed, update both the sum and the count.

steps.title: Average after replacement
steps.prompt: The average of 6 numbers is 15. One number 10 is replaced by 22. What is the new average?
steps.explanation: Old total = 6×15 = 90. New total = 90−10+22 = 102. New average = 102/6 = 17.

steps.title: Weighted average
steps.content: When groups have different sizes, average the combined total—not the two averages directly. Combined average = (n₁a₁+n₂a₂)/(n₁+n₂).
steps.example: 10 students average 60; 20 students average 75. Combined average = (600+1500)/30 = 70.

questions.prompt: The average of 8 values is 12. What is their sum?
The average of 4 numbers is 20. A fifth number 30 is added. What is the new average?
questions.explanation: Old total 80; new total 110; new average 110/5 = 22.

questions.prompt: 10 students average 50 marks and 20 students average 65. Find the combined average.
The average age of 5 people is 24. A person aged 30 joins. What is the new average?
questions.explanation: Old total 120; new total 150; count 6; average 25.

learning_objectives: Calculate arithmetic mean from a data set.
Find a missing value from a known average.
Update an average when an item is added or removed.

common_misconceptions.misconception: Adding a large value always increases an average by that value.
common_misconceptions.correction: The new average depends on both the old total and the new count.

common_misconceptions.misconception: The average of two groups is always the mean of their averages.
common_misconceptions.correction: Weight each group's average by its number of observations.

common_misconceptions.misconception: Removing an item leaves the average unchanged.
common_misconceptions.correction: Recalculate the total and count after removal.

worked_examples.title: Find the average
worked_examples.explanation: Mean equals total divided by count.

worked_examples.title: Find a missing mark
worked_examples.input: Average of 5 students is 70; four marks total 270
worked_examples.explanation: Convert the average back into a total before finding a missing value.

worked_examples.title: Combine two groups
worked_examples.explanation: A combined average must weight each group by its size.

company_applications.practice: Use total-and-count reasoning for missing values.
Calculate combined averages with group sizes.
Avoid averaging group averages without weights.

srs_cards.question: What are the key ideas in Averages?
srs_cards.answer: Calculate arithmetic mean from a data set. Find a missing value from a known average. Update an average when an item is added or removed. Solve weighted-average situations.

srs_cards.question: Name a common mistake in Averages.
srs_cards.answer: The new average depends on both the old total and the new count.
